# Plan: `#include "rbtree.h"` in `src/rbtree.c`

## Context

`src/rbtree.c` currently defines `struct rbtree` with a field of type
`rb_value_free_fn`, but that type is declared only in `include/rbtree.h`, which
the file never includes. As written the translation unit will not compile once
it is actually built (`make test`). Beyond fixing that symbol, including the
header is what ties this implementation file to the graded contract: it is the
single source of the public types and function prototypes, so the compiler can
check that the definitions in `rbtree.c` match what callers and the test suite
expect.

## What `#include` actually does

- `#include` is a **preprocessor** directive. Before the compiler proper runs,
  the preprocessor replaces the `#include "rbtree.h"` line with the full text of
  `include/rbtree.h`. It is literal textual substitution.
- **Quote form vs angle form**: `"rbtree.h"` searches the directory of the
  current file first, then the `-I` paths, then system paths. `<rbtree.h>` skips
  that first step. Convention: use `"rbtree.h"` for a header that belongs to this
  project. It resolves via `-Iinclude` in `Makefile:2`.
- **Header guard**: `include/rbtree.h` is wrapped in `#ifndef RBTREE_H /
  #define RBTREE_H / ... / #endif`, so if it is included more than once in a
  translation unit the body is expanded only the first time.
- After expansion, `rbtree.c` gains, in order:
  - `#include <stddef.h>` (transitively) — the canonical definition of `size_t`
    used by the `size` field.
  - `typedef struct rbtree rbtree_t;` — an **incomplete-type** forward
    declaration of the *same* `struct rbtree` tag that `rbtree.c` defines fully.
    The two are compatible; the `.c` file completes the type. This is the opaque
    pointer pattern: callers only ever see `rbtree_t *`.
  - `typedef void (*rb_value_free_fn)(void *value);` — the function-pointer type
    the struct's `value_free` field needs. **This is the symbol that is
    currently missing.**
  - Prototypes for `rb_create`, `rb_insert`, `rb_find`, `rb_delete`, `rb_size`,
    `rb_foreach`, `rb_validate`, `rb_destroy`. With these visible, when those
    functions are implemented later the compiler enforces that each definition's
    signature matches the contract (a mismatch is a `-Werror` failure rather
    than a silent link-time surprise).

## Change

Single-line addition to `src/rbtree.c`. Place the project header immediately
after the standard-library includes:

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

#include "rbtree.h"
```

Rationale for position: minimal diff, and groups system headers together. (Some
style guides put a module's own header first so that any missing transitive
include in the header is caught immediately — either is defensible here; the
current file already leads with `<stdio.h>`/`<stdlib.h>`.)

No other edits. `rb_color_t`, `struct rb_node`, and the full `struct rbtree`
definition do not conflict with anything the header introduces.

## Files

- `src/rbtree.c` — add `#include "rbtree.h"` (1 line, plus a blank separator).

- `make test` — must compile (this is the concrete proof the missing
  `rb_value_free_fn` symbol is resolved) and pass. Note the suite also links
  `tests/test_rbtree.c` / `tests/fuzz.c`, which are currently empty, so "passes"
  today just means "builds and runs an empty suite".
- `make asan` and `make memcheck` — per the project rule that a change is done
  only when all three pass. Show output for each.

Dependency-free harness (no framework in the repo): a `CHECK(cond)` macro that logs `FILE:LINE` + expression and bumps a `failures` counter; `main` returns `EXIT_FAILURE` if any failed.

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `Makefile` | tabs on the 9 recipe lines (the approved fix — diff shown above) |

## One gotcha to know

`make asan` leaves ASan-instrumented binaries in `build/`. `make memcheck` pulls in `all`, which sees them as up-to-date and *doesn't* rebuild — so valgrind then runs an ASan binary and crashes (that's the SIGSEGV you'd have seen if I'd chained them). **Run `make clean` between `asan` and `memcheck`.** Pre-existing Makefile design; I left it alone since you approved only the tab fix. I can make `memcheck: clean all` if you want it robust.
